protocol: open_world_plan_review.typ:569 ('KAPSO 的正门 ... 可配置关闭，但 Bash 侧门关不掉'), independent_review.typ:320 (D15)
study_verdict_scope: conditional on setting one config key for the codex lane (measured: `agent_specific.sandbox=workspace-write` closes the shell network end to end WHILE the model call still completes, rc=0 -- evidence/11_kapso_lane_closed.json) and on an external network cut for the claude lane, which has no CLI-level sandbox and where the only config-level move (banning Bash) closes the lane by deleting the capability it exists to use.
verdict_note: The Bash side door was not driven end to end by a live model turn through KAPSO's own campaign loop; what is proven is the argv of the lane commands KAPSO launches (real adapter code) plus the CLI sandbox behaviour they select.

observed.evidence: lane argv emitted by KAPSO's own adapters: codex lane -> ['codex','--search','exec','--sandbox','danger-full-access',...]; claude lane -> ['claude','-p','--dangerously-skip-permissions',...,'--allowedTools','Edit,Read,Write,Bash',...] and get_capabilities()['sandbox'] == False (evidence/04_seam_kapso.log). The codex lane's posture was additionally run END TO END on the real model lane: `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (same posture as the lane's danger-full-access) -> canary egress=OPEN (evidence/09_e2e_codex_bypass.jsonl), while `-s workspace-write` -> egress=BLOCKED (evidence/08_e2e_codex_workspace_write.jsonl).

mechanisms.why: The named front doors are config-gated and can be turned off (web_search, implementation_web, ideation_gates/implementation_gates, research role disabled). Config alone is explicitly NOT proof (plan:569), and at least one path overrides the knob: the ensemble selector session is launched with web_search=True hardcoded (search_strategies/generic/ideation.py:794), and the researcher path goes through cli_inference.llm_completion_with_web_search (researcher.py:189 -> cli_inference.py:210).
mechanisms.probe_status: NOT PROBED dynamically; a config-only closure claim for these paths would be a false green.

mechanisms.study_verdict: OPEN as shipped; CLOSED by one config key (agent_specific.sandbox=workspace-write, web_search=false)
mechanisms.schema_verdict_scope: verdict for the codex lane when that key is set, as driven for A0/A1; the shipped preset (no key) remains egress_detected
mechanisms.measured: executed end to end with a real model turn on the lane argv built by KAPSO's own CodexCodingAgent._exec_command: rc=0 (model call completed), the in-lane shell tool ran and persisted `LANE_PROBE ... local=ok egress=BLOCKED` (evidence/11_kapso_lane_closed.json, 34.8s). Control through the same machinery with the shipped default: `codex --search exec --sandbox danger-full-access ...` -> rc=0, egress=OPEN (evidence/11b_kapso_lane_open.json).
mechanisms.why: As shipped, the lane argv is `codex --search exec --sandbox danger-full-access ...` (agents.yaml:188-189 -> codex_agent.py:117, 187-189): an unsandboxed Bash tool plus the provider-side web-search tool. The adapter accepts a lane-level sandbox ('agent_specific.sandbox', codex_agent.py:117) -- KAPSO's strategy simply never passes one (implementation.py:212-231 sets env/mcp/web_search/timeout but no sandbox), although the same tree uses it elsewhere. Setting it is a configuration change to the adapter's lane spec, not a code change.
mechanisms.authority_note: supersedes the KAPSO workstream's lane_probes.codex_workspace_write, which timed out (rc=124, command_ran=false) and therefore never observed this posture; see closure.reconciliation.json
mechanisms.false_claim_in_protocol: The protocol says KAPSO has 'no lane-level sandbox parameter'. That is inaccurate at the adapter level: the parameter exists and is used elsewhere in the same tree (learning/graders/frame.py:72, learning/codify_run.py:249,273, learning/behavior.py:122 all set agent_specific['sandbox']='workspace-write'). It is the GENERIC search strategy's lane construction that omits it.
mechanisms.caution: the closed posture disables the codex lane's `--search`; the model must not be able to re-enable web search through another config layer -- re-probe at run time (adapter contract section 7) rather than trusting the key once set

executed_probe.end_to_end: on the real model lane: `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (the lane's posture) -> canary egress=OPEN (evidence/09_e2e_codex_bypass.jsonl); `-s workspace-write` -> egress=BLOCKED (evidence/08_e2e_codex_workspace_write.jsonl)
executed_probe.note: the CLI sandbox behaviour is shared with every codex-driven lane

mechanisms.why: Lane argv is `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions ... --allowedTools Edit,Read,Write,Bash --disallowedTools ScheduleWakeup` (claude_code_agent.py:1182, 1208, 1213) and the adapter's own capability report says sandbox: False (claude_code_agent.py:1331). The CLI help itself warns the mode is 'Recommended only for sandboxes with no internet access'. No CLI-level sandbox exists to turn on.
mechanisms.available_but_unusable_knobs: `claude --restricted` removes the code-running tools (Bash/REPL) and WebFetch entirely; KAPSO's own route is to add Bash to agent_specific.disallowed_tools. Both close the door by DELETING the tool the coding lane exists to use, so neither is a viable closure for an algorithm-improvement runtime -- and a lane without Bash cannot run KAPSO's registered evaluation through its own machinery, which is what A0.1 rests on.
mechanisms.reconciliation: the KAPSO workstream's record lists 'claude lane: agent_specific.disallowed_tools removes Bash' under lane_closure_by and marks the channel closed_by_config. Its own probe shows why that is not a runtime closure: the in-lane command never ran (command_ran=false) and the agent replied that the Bash tool is absent -- an ABSENT tool was observed, never a DENIED network attempt. See closure.reconciliation.json; this workstream's verdict for the channel is CONDITIONAL.
mechanisms.probe_status: The lane command class can only be constrained from outside: unshare -rn / docker --internal (probe-proven to block egress, evidence/01_external_isolation.log).

mechanisms.runtime_path: cli_inference codex sessions (roles: research and friends)
mechanisms.why: These sessions run under inference.default.sandbox = read-only (config.yaml:29) which blocks shell egress, BUT the web-search front door they use is the provider-side web_search tool (cli_inference.py:104-117, 193-210) which the sandbox does not cover. Closing requires web_search: false for the role.
mechanisms.provider_caveat: PROBED: on this machine's provider (custom zjapi relay, wire_api=responses) a real model turn answered NO_WEB_SEARCH_TOOL even with `-c web_search="live"` (evidence/10b_e2e_websearch_live.jsonl). The front door is currently shut by the PROVIDER, not by configuration -- provider-dependent, must be re-probed if the provider changes.
mechanisms.flag_position_note: KAPSO places `--search` before `exec` (`codex --search exec ...`, codex_agent.py:186-189), which is the accepted position; `codex exec --search` is rejected by the CLI ('unexpected argument', evidence/10_e2e_websearch_live.jsonl -- that run failed for this reason and was replaced by 10b).

sharp_edges: External network cut (unshare -rn) severs HOST-LOCAL services: the model relay at 127.0.0.1:15722 answers 200 on the host and is unreachable inside the cut, and docker --internal + host-gateway does not restore it (evidence/02_host_loopback_cut.log). So for the claude lane (or any lane 'closed' by an external cut) the model endpoint must be reachable from inside the barrier -- e.g. a sibling container on the internal network -- while the orchestrator stays outside.
Wrap only the candidate-execution channel, never the orchestrator: the orchestrator legitimately needs the model endpoint.
KAPSO's own campaign loop, git worktrees and the registered-evaluation path live outside the lane process; wrapping the lane must not cut the evaluation channel (E*) or the campaign inbox.
unverified: No KAPSO campaign was run: the lane command is KAPSO's own argv, executed end to end with a real model turn (evidence/11, 11b), but the surrounding campaign machinery (worktrees, inbox, registered-evaluation trigger) was not exercised by this workstream.
Whether every front door (gates, knowledge_search backends) is genuinely off at run time in the adapter's configuration.
The claude lane: not driven end to end here (claude's configured model id is reported expired by the CLI). Its verdict does not depend on that -- the lane has no sandbox either way.
verdict_summary: top-level `verdict=inconclusive` (treated as NOT closed) because KAPSO's DEFAULT lane is claude_code, which has no CLI sandbox and is not closed by configuration. The codex lane IS measured closed with a live model call when agent_specific.sandbox=workspace-write is set; choose that lane, or cut the network, and the runtime is closed.
